Stomach contents of North-East Atlantic fishes (ICES, 2020-2024)

Source: R/data.R
ices_diet.Rd

A public extract of the ICES Stomach Content Database: 9,639 prey records from 4,231 stomachs of 22 predator species caught in the North Sea, the Skagerrak-Kattegat and the Baltic Sea by national trawl and acoustic surveys, 2020-2024 (mostly 2022-2024). One row per prey record, in the format DietView expects, with the stomach-level variables repeated on each row. Use it with the frozen lineage ices_lineage (taxonomy = "table").

Usage

ices_diet

Format

A data frame with 9,639 rows and 28 columns:

stomach_id

Stomach (one predator individual) identifier.

prey_aphia_id

WoRMS AphiaID of the prey; NA for unidentified material and non-food items.

prey_name

Prey name as resolved in WoRMS, "Unidentified material", or the non-food item.

item_type

"prey", "unidentified" or "non_food".

digestion_stage

ICES digestion code (0, 1, 2), NA when not recorded.

digestion_label

Readable digestion stage: "0 pristine", "1 affected", "2 skeletal remains" or "not recorded". The labels are inferred from the older ICES format, whose three classes match the shares of codes 0, 1 and 2; check them against the ICES vocabulary.

prey_count

Number of prey individuals in the record.

prey_weight_g

Prey weight (g).

prey_length_cm

Prey length (cm).

haul_id, country, survey

Haul, reporting country and survey.

year, month, quarter

Date of the haul.

lat, lon, ices_rectangle, depth_m

Position and depth of the haul.

region

"North Sea", "Skagerrak-Kattegat" or "Baltic Sea".

predator_aphia_id, predator_latin, predator_common

Predator AphiaID, scientific and English name.

n_fish_pooled

Number of fish in the stomach sample (1 or 2; NA when not reported).

length_cm, weight_g

Predator length (cm) and weight (g).

stomach_empty, regurgitated

ICES flags (1 = yes, 0 = no).

Source

ICES Stomach Content Database, ICES, Copenhagen (https://stomachdata.ices.dk), as extracted in the R package stomachr (Lindmark 2026, https://github.com/maxlindmark/stomachr), which also built the WoRMS classification used in ices_lineage. ICES data are free to use provided the source is acknowledged; see the ICES data policy.

Details

The data are kept close to the ICES export, so they show what real stomach-content data look like:

  • prey are identified to very uneven depth (species, family, "Crustacea", "Pisces", or nothing at all: 1,553 records are unidentified material);

  • 67 records are non-food items (sand, stones, plastic, wood), flagged by item_type == "non_food";

  • about 1,000 records are Nematoda, which in fish stomachs are mostly parasites rather than prey;

  • the digestion stage is missing for about a third of the records;

  • 17 sampled stomachs pool two fish (n_fish_pooled == 2 in ices_stomachs), 7 of them with prey records here.

Deciding what to keep is part of any analysis; the article "Case study: a complete analysis of public ICES stomach data" walks through it.

Two kinds of correction were made when the data were built (data-raw/ices_data.R in the package sources): rows that only mark an empty stomach in the ICES export (no prey, weight, count or digestion) were dropped, and two unit errors in the predator variables were fixed (Belgian lengths reported in mm, Danish individual weights reported in kg). Prey weights are in grams and prey lengths in cm throughout.

See also

ices_stomachs for every sampled stomach, empty ones included; ices_lineage for the taxonomy.

Examples

head(ices_diet[, c("stomach_id", "predator_common", "prey_name", "prey_weight_g")])
#>   stomach_id predator_common             prey_name prey_weight_g
#> 1    S167767         Whiting Unidentified material          0.03
#> 2    S167777         Whiting Unidentified material          0.07
#> 3    S167777         Whiting Unidentified material          0.06
#> 4    S167777         Whiting Unidentified material          0.01
#> 5    S167769         Whiting Unidentified material          0.20
#> 6    S167780         Whiting Unidentified material          1.72
table(ices_diet$item_type)
#> 
#>     non_food         prey unidentified 
#>           67         8019         1553 

spec <- dv_spec(predator = "predator_common", predator_latin = "predator_latin",
                stomach = "stomach_id", prey_id = "prey_aphia_id",
                prey_name = "prey_name", weight = "prey_weight_g",
                digestion = "digestion_label", covariates = c("region", "quarter"))
cod <- ices_diet[ices_diet$predator_common == "Atlantic cod" &
                   ices_diet$item_type != "non_food", ]
prep <- dv_prepare(cod, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage,
                   verbose = FALSE)
dv_rank_table(dv_tree(prep), "Class")
#>           label value_item value_occ     pct_occ  value_w        pct_w
